metadata.title: Drive Coach iOS — Apoorv Mahajan
metadata.description: A SwiftUI driving-confidence app for new drivers, borrowing Apple Health's September 2026 redesign patterns — rolling confidence score, For You coaching cards, and a six-category skill overview.

blocks.text: help new drivers see their own growth clearly enough to actually build confidence behind the wheel?

controls.heading: Role
controls.bodyText: End-to-end: product design, SwiftUI build, data model

blocks.text: Designed and built the whole SwiftUI app solo: the data model, the scoring engine, and all four tabs.

The same ScoreBand/ConfidenceBand vocabulary drives the ring, the trend badges, the skill bars, and the streak banner — so the whole app reads as one coherent language, not four separately-designed screens.
Borrowed the Shape, Not the Skin
Read Apple’s September 2026 Health redesign closely, then re-derived the pattern for driving:

items: Readiness’s 0-10 score + four-tier language became a rolling Confidence Score
The Insights tab’s “For You” mix of a win and a focus area became two coaching cards, not just a list of problems
The Longevity tab’s all-dimensions-at-once view became the Skill Overview bars

blocks.text: Reached for iOS 17’s native motion APIs instead of hand-rolled animation plumbing:

items: contentTransition(.numericText()) on every score and delta
scrollTransition fade/scale on cards as they enter the viewport
viewAligned scroll snapping on the Recent Drives strip, spring-scale press states on every card

blocks.text: Extracted concrete patterns from Apple’s own announcement rather than guessing at “Health-style design”:

items: Baseline-relative language (“Trending Up,” not just a raw number)
A card mix of celebration and focus, never only problems
A one-line “why this number” explanation under every score

blocks.text: Every screen reuses the same ScoreBand/ConfidenceBand color-and-label system, so a ring, a badge, and a bar all mean the same thing at a glance.

A recency-weighted rolling average across the last five drives, mapped to a four-tier band: Keep Practicing, Building Confidence, Driving Well, Road Ready.
One rough drive doesn’t crash the number, and one great one doesn’t inflate it — the same shape as Apple’s own Readiness score.

blocks.alt: Drive Coach Insights tab showing the Confidence Score ring and band

blocks.text: One win, one focus, every time
The engine compares each scenario’s last three drives against the three before that, then surfaces the biggest improvement and the biggest dip — never just a list of what went wrong.
Up 5 points over your last few drives. Keep it up.
Add one more car length of following distance on faster roads.

All six scenarios — Speed, Braking, Signal, Following Distance, Turns, Night Driving — compared at once before drilling into any single one’s trend line.
Same idea as Health’s Longevity tab showing every dimension side by side instead of one metric at a time.

blocks.alt: Drive Coach Trends tab showing the Skill Overview bars and a category trend line

blocks.text:
Score digits count up instead of jump-cutting, cards fade and settle in as they scroll into view, and the Recent Drives strip snaps card-to-card instead of drifting to a stop mid-card.
None of it is custom animation code — all native iOS 17 SwiftUI: contentTransition, scrollTransition, and viewAligned scroll targets.

blocks.alt: Drive Coach Summary tab showing the latest drive score ring and AI Drive Review card

blocks.text: The rolling Confidence Score turns “am I getting better?” into a number and a plain-language band, the same trick Apple’s Readiness score plays for workout recovery.
Coaching that celebrates, not just corrects.
For You always pairs a win with a focus area — matching Apple Health’s own encouraging tone instead of a list of what a new driver did wrong.
Numeric count-ups, scroll-linked fades, and view-aligned snapping run on native iOS 17 SwiftUI APIs — no custom animation plumbing to maintain.
